english.title: Send unmarked / dangerous goods on railway
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) sent by rail belonging to the **(..SPECIFY THE COMPANY..) goods that in the judgement of the **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..) were of a dangerous nature, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..), without

(A)_[distinctly marking the nature of the goods on the outside of the package containing the same]_
(B)_[giving notice in writing to the servant of the said **(..SPECIFY THE COMPANY..) with whom the goods were left at the time of sending]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 105 of the Railway Clauses Consolidation Act 1845.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

english.notes:
(i) In Scotland this offence contravenes Section 98 of the Railway Clauses Consolidation Act 1845.
(ii) Guilty knowledge by the sender must be proved. Hearne v Garton (1859) 2EandE 66.
(iii) This section also allows the company to require inspection of the contents of any parcel if they suspect that there may be goods of a dangerous nature within. Railway undertakers and not the court are to decide whether a particular article is dangerous. (North Eastern Railway v Reckitt and Sons Ltd (1913) 109 LT 327) and (Midland Railway v Brotherton and Co Ltd (1920) 36 TLR 679).
